the combination of microcaloralimetry and rRNA-SIP allows the detection of distinct phases of substrate degradation in a very sensitive way.

the combination of microcalarimetry with ribosome-based SIP allows the identification of active bacteria in complex communities and the identification of distinct phases in microbial metabolism in a highly sensitive manner.

microcalorimetric analysis is an excellent tool to follow substrate turnover, and ribosome-based SIP allows identifying the responsible species in a very sensitive way.
microcalorimetric measurements are a powerful tool for studying anaerobic processes in anoxic sediments.
microcalorimetric measurements are a valuable tool in microbial ecology to follow microbial activities in the field, in the lab, and in combination with stable-isotope probing.

the combination of microcalarimetry and ribosomal-SIP is a promising approach to identify active microorganisms in complex environments.

microcalorimetric measurements of heat production in combination with ribosome-based SIP is an excellent tool for identifying the active bacteria in a community and for studying the temporal succession of substrate utilization in anoxic sediments.
